copy_failed: Copy failed — select the text and copy it
services_turns_note: Turns include suspended turns and retries, so they can exceed completed + failed. Statistics cover the default window.
shell_auth_off: Auth is off — everyone is cluster-admin
shell_expires: Session expires in {minutes} min — log in again to continue.
shell_no_sections: This key can invoke services but cannot see the console sections.
palette_description: Go to a section or paste an invocation or deployment ID.
login_help: Paste a key (cf_…). It is exchanged for a session cookie and never stored in the browser.
not_found_body: There is nothing at this address.
forbidden_body: Your key's role cannot open this page.
overview_throughput_empty: No history yet — hourly summaries are written every minute.
attention_drained: {id} has no pinned invocations — safe to remove
onboarding_step_run: Start a service with the SDK — for example, the TypeScript sample:
onboarding_step_register: Paste the URL your service listens on:
onboarding_step_docs: Then follow docs/quickstart.md to send your first invocation.
filter_id_invalid: An ID is up to 48 hex characters.
filter_type_value: Type a value, then press Enter.
invocations_empty_body: Try another view or remove a filter.
why_title: Why it is in this state
why_paused_attempts: Paused after running out of attempts — resume it once the cause is fixed.
why_queued_behind: Waiting for the lock of {object} — {pos} of {n} in line; held by
why_queued: Waiting in the queue of {object} — {pos} of {n} in line
why_holds_lock: Holds the lock of {object}; waiting behind it: {n}
detail_live_off: Auto-refresh is off because this invocation has more than {n} journal entries. Reload to update.
invocation_bad_id: An invocation ID is 48 hex characters.
invocation_missing: No invocation with this ID is visible to your key.
log_polling: Polling mode — durable log lines only, refreshed every 2 s.
log_live: Live — new lines appear as they are written (including ones not yet durable).
log_ended: Log sealed — every line is shown.
log_connecting: Connecting to the node leading this invocation…
log_durable_ended: Durable log lines — the invocation has ended.
tree_empty: No calls from or to other invocations.
deployment_remove_body: Removes {id}. No service uses it as its current revision and no invocation is pinned to it.
action_forbidden: Your key's role cannot do this.
action_throttled: The node is busy (429). Try again in a moment.
action_not_leader: This range is led by another node ({leader}), and the node serving the console couldn't reach it. Nothing was changed — try again in a moment.
action_no_leader: This range has no leader right now (an election, split or merge is in progress). Try again in a moment.
action_ambiguous: The node leading this range didn't answer in time. The action may have run — check the status before trying again.
bulk_not_leader: the node leading this range couldn't be reached — nothing was changed
action_cancel_soft_body: Sends a cancel signal; the handler's own cleanup runs and the invocation ends with its own failure. Needs the SDK to be running.
action_cancel_hard_body: Ends the invocation as failed (572) without waiting for the SDK. Side effects of a turn already in flight still happen.
action_purge_body: Deletes the journal, state and idempotency key of this ended invocation. This cannot be undone.
action_restart_body: Starts a new invocation that reuses the journal before the chosen step (results of runs there are kept) and runs again from that step.
action_replay_body: Runs the existing journal against a deployment without committing anything.
action_migrate_body: Moves this unfinished invocation to another deployment. A replay check must match first unless you force it.
action_signal_body: Delivers a named signal to this invocation (what ctx.signal(name) waits for). Delivering the same name again does nothing.
signal_value_hint: Empty sends the signal without a value (not the same as null).
bulk_dialog_body: Runs in pages of up to 1,000 invocations. Each invocation gets exactly the single-invocation action; one failure does not stop the rest.
bulk_estimate: This is a large batch — it takes about {s} seconds. Keep this tab open.
select_page: Select all rows on this page
schedule_cron_raw: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday.
schedule_trigger_body: Starts one run of {name} now, outside its timetable.
schedule_delete_body: Deletes the schedule {name}. Runs already started are not touched.
schedules_empty_body: Create one here, or from your app with PUT /schedules/<name>.
schedules_partial: Some nodes did not answer ({nodes}) — their schedules are missing from this list.
workflow_not_started: No run for this key yet
workflow_not_started_body: Its run would have the ID {id}…
workflow_waiting: Promises the run is waiting on
promise_already: Promise {name} already had a result — nothing changed
awakeable_owner: Open the invocation waiting on it
run_body: Sends one invocation (fire-and-forget) and opens it.
deploy_intro: Registers the new version without routing any new invocation to it. Compare, replay-check, then move each service yourself.
deploy_uri: Endpoint URI of the new version
deploy_service_same: no change to handlers or contract
deploy_handlers_removed: Handlers removed: {names} — calls to them will fail after the move
deploy_replay_body: Replays up to 20 unfinished invocations of each service on the new version — read-only, nothing is committed.
deploy_move_done: Every service already runs this version.
deploy_move_confirm: New invocations of {services} will run on the new version. Each move only happens if the service still points where it did when you loaded this page.
deploy_drained: Drained — no unfinished invocation left on it.
deploy_pinned_left: {n} unfinished invocations still run on it
deploy_migrate_matching: Migrate the ones that replay cleanly
deploy_rollback_body: Moves {services} back to {id}. Only happens if they still point at the new version.
deploy_delete_body: Removes deployment {id}. It no longer serves any service and has no unfinished invocation.

sample_2: Throughput, success and latency, last hour
sample_6: Longest queues and what blocks them

query_no_chart: No chart for this result: it needs a time column and numbers, or a text column and a number.
query_chart_label: Line chart of {y} over {x}. The table view has every value.
query_chart_dropped: Not drawn (one axis, at most 4 lines): {cols}
query_chart_top: First {n} rows shown — the table has all of them.
query_render_cap: Showing the first {n} rows — the CSV has all of them.
query_budget_hint: Add a LIMIT, or filter on an indexed column (service, class, created_at, id) so it reads less.
stats_body: The last {n} queries the console sent from this tab: server time, read units, browser time, partial results and errors.
stats_empty: No queries yet in this tab
sample_3: Completed and failed per hour, last 30 days
usage_empty_body: Each node writes an hourly summary about once a minute — check back shortly.
usage_no_price_note: No token prices are set, so costs are not computed. Token prices are set by whoever operates this cluster (cairn-ctl pricing set).
usage_chart_status_label: Line chart of completed and failed invocations per hour. The table below has totals per handler.
usage_chart_cu_label: Line chart of compute units per hour. The table below has totals per handler.
usage_tokens_empty: No tokens recorded in this range. Spans with token counts in $trace show up here.
usage_chart_tokens_label: Line chart of input and output tokens per hour. The table below has totals per model.
usage_chart_cost_label: Line chart of token cost per hour in US dollars. The table below has totals per model.
slow_body: Runs that took longer than the tenant's slow threshold, still in each node's memory, newest first.
slow_partial: Some nodes did not answer ({nodes}) — their slow runs are missing.
archive_body: Purged invocations, read back from the archive: final status, output and journal.
archive_verified_ok: The record matches its hash chain.
archive_verified_none: No hash chain on this tenant.
rules_propagating: Still propagating: {behind} of {n} ranges run an older version (about 2 s).
rules_empty_body: Without rules nothing is capped. Add one to limit concurrency or the CU rate of a scope, limit key or tenant.
rule_pattern_hint: scope, scope/l1 or scope/l1/l2; each part a value or *. The more specific rule wins.
rule_rate_hint: Compute units per second — a number, or unlimited.
rule_burst_hint: CU that can build up; defaults to the rate.
rule_merge_hint: Saving merges into the existing rule. Clearing a field removes that limit; unlimited lifts it explicitly.
rule_merge_detail: An empty field that had no value stays unset. Clearing a field that had a value removes that limit, and the broader rule's limit applies again.
rule_star_warning: * is not a shared pool: every matching scope gets its own budget of this size.
rule_err_number: Must be a whole number (≥ 0), or unlimited.
rule_err_tenant_concurrency: A tenant cap only takes a rate.
rule_disabled_toast: Disabled {target} — a broader rule may apply now
rule_delete_body: Deletes {target}. Counters it capped fall back to the next matching rule, or to no cap.
flow_limits_empty: No counter is in use right now.
flow_queues_empty: No queue has work right now.
settings_cluster_only: API keys, tenant settings, captures and pricing need a cluster-admin key.
thresholds_body: When the Overview flags a service. Saved in this browser only.
thresholds_not_saved: This browser blocks storage — thresholds were not saved
keys_empty_body: The bootstrap key (CAIRNFLOW_ADMIN_KEY) is never listed.
key_new_body: The secret is shown once, right after you create the key.
key_secret_once: Copy the secret now — it is shown only this once and cannot be recovered. Only its hash is stored.
key_roles_disabled: The cluster has not enabled the view/provision key roles yet — an operator must run cairn-ctl cluster enable-key-roles first.
key_revoke_body: Revokes key {id}. Requests with it are refused as soon as every node has applied this.
key_revoke_self: This console is signed in with this key — you will be signed out.
key_revoked_pending: Revoked {id} — not yet confirmed by {nodes}, they apply it within one refresh
tenant_hash_chain_hint: A hash chain applies to invocations created after the change.
tenant_quarantine_hint: Quarantine stops a handler that keeps failing from hurting the rest of the tenant. Empty = node default.
tenant_quarantine_detail: Modes: off disables detection; observe only reports it; cooldown allows one concurrent run per range; hold pauses its new invocations until you resume them after deploying a fix. The rule attempts/invocations/seconds (e.g. 20/5/300) trips after that many failed attempts across that many invocations with no success in the window.
capture_body: Saves a bundle of the next matching invocations (journal, state, deployment) when they finish or pause — to reproduce a failure outside the cluster.
pricing_body: Price per 1 M tokens, used for the cost in Usage. Set by whoever operates this cluster (cairn-ctl pricing set).
pricing_empty: No prices set — costs show as 0.
keyspace_caption: Ranges across the key space, colored by leader
cluster_pick_range: Pick a range on the bar to split it or merge it with its right neighbour.
cluster_split_body: Splits range {range} at the key below (by default the middle of its key space) on the node that leads it. Invocations keep running; the range briefly pauses while it seals.
cluster_split_at_hint: First key of the right half, within {start}–{end} (the start key itself is not allowed). Empty = the middle, {mid}.
cluster_split_at_format: The split key must be exactly 16 hex digits.
cluster_split_at_outside: The split key must be after {start} and no later than {end}.
cluster_merge_body: Merges ranges {left} and {right} into one. Both briefly pause while they seal.
cluster_no_suggestions: No suggestions — no range is hot or large.
cluster_no_ops: No split or merge on this node yet.
cluster_no_wal: No shared WAL log is alive (nodes use per-range WAL).
cluster_trash_hint: Deleted customer data waits here before it is purged; restore it with cairn-ctl trash.
cluster_gc_plan: Can be collected: {eligible} · held back: {blocked} · {bytes} bytes · barriers: {barriers}
cluster_gc_hint: Read-only plan — collection runs in the background and only deletes what it can prove unused.
rules_star_warning: A rule with `*` is not one shared pool: it gives EACH matching scope its own budget. Two scopes under a `*` rule with concurrency=1000 can run 2000 invocations at once.
workflows_intro: One run per key. Pick a run below, or type a key to open it.
objects_intro: One object per key: its state and the invocations it holds. Pick one below, or type a key to open it.
workflows_none_body: Register a deployment that has a workflow service, and its runs show up here.
workflow_runs_empty_body: Each key you send to its run handler starts one run.
objects_none_body: Register a deployment that has a virtual object, and its keys show up here.
objects_keys_empty_body: A key shows up here once something calls the object with it.
kpi_no_turns: No turns in the recent window
streams_durable_only: Durable streams only (ctx.stream with durable: true), refreshed every 2 s. Temporary streams live only in the leader's memory and are not shown here yet.
streams_live: Live — records appear as they are written.
streams_sealed: Stream sealed — every record is shown.
streams_live_hint: Durable streams of this invocation; records stream live while it runs.
streams_empty_body: Records the handler writes to a durable stream show here once they are committed.
trace_empty_body: This invocation recorded no trace. Spans come from ctx.trace.span, or from handlers declared with trace: "runtime" (one span per turn and per ctx.run).
trace_start_lost: Its start record was not persisted (the node died mid-span); the start shown is its end.
timeline_estimated_title: Re-run on this attempt: the runtime did not see it start, so this is an upper bound (from the start of the turn).
timeline_entries: Journal steps (select to highlight their runs)
timeline_enable_runtime: Turn on trace: "runtime" for this handler to get a per-step timeline (one lane per attempt, one row per ctx.run). Until then, only the invocation's milestones:
query_recent_empty: Queries you run show up here (this browser only).
query_start_body: Pick a sample — it runs right away — or write SQL above and press Ctrl/⌘ + Enter. Tables lists every table and column.
objects_count_cap: First {n} objects — filter by key to narrow
login_sso_help: You will be sent to your sign-in service and brought back here.
login_sso_error_access_denied: Your account does not have access to this environment. Ask an owner of the organization to grant it.
login_sso_error_revoked: Your access to this environment was just changed. Wait a minute, then sign in again.
login_sso_error_issuer_unavailable: The sign-in service cannot be reached right now. Try again shortly, or use an API key.
login_sso_error_invalid_state: That sign-in attempt expired or was started in another tab. Start again.
login_sso_error_token_rejected: The sign-in service's answer was not accepted. Try again; if it keeps happening, contact your administrator.
login_sso_error_not_configured: Single sign-on is not set up for this address.
login_sso_error_other: Sign-in did not complete ({code}). Try again.
limits_intro: Set by your plan or the cluster operator. Requests over a limit are rejected with a clear error.
audit_body: Who changed what in this tenant: deployments, keys, cancels and restarts, schedules, sign-ins, and requests refused for lack of permission.
audit_truncated_title: Showing only part of this range
audit_truncated_body: The server stops at 1,000 records per request. Choose a shorter time range or filter by actor or action to see the rest.
audit_empty: No audit records in this range
audit_source_noop: Requests that changed nothing, grouped per minute
deployment_missing_body: It was removed, or the ID is wrong.
invocations_none_yet_body: Invocations appear here once a deployment receives its first call.
